question: to the Commission David Casa (PPE) Subject:

On 17 January 2025, the European Banking Authority published Q&A 2022_6336, authored by the Commission, concerning the interpretation of the definition of electronic money. There are concerns that the Q&A’s narrow interpretation of the contractual relationship between issuers and merchants, and of the transfer of e-money to merchants, may not take sufficient account of the way in which four-party payment schemes function and, if applied to such schemes, could prevent such products from continuing to operate. In view of the above: 1.

How does the Commission consider the interpretation set out in Q&A 2022_6336, in particular the requirement for the transfer of e-money to the merchant, to be compatible with the E-Money Directive and the relevant case law?
Is the Commission considering clarifying that e-money products operating through fourparty payment schemes should not be regarded as falling within the scope of Q&A 2022_6336?
